parts.note: something arranged is set, as a table is set or a date is set
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone books a hospital appointment to stand in for a man called Abel.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis says Eve bore a third son to take the murdered Abel's place, his name meaning 'appointed'; 'appointment' backs that up rather than adding letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the third son of Adam and Eve was born after Cain killed Abel and was seen as given in his stead.

clue.text: The rub of tin on silver

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so the tin symbol comes first

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, from Latin argentum

explanation.surface: Someone describes rubbing a tin object against a silver one.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The rub' is the hitch or difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub', a synonym for a catch or obstacle.

definitions.note: the definition is phrased as a past description; the answer is the name of that old penalty

indicators.note: a preparation of rice suggests the letters of the word being made up into something new

explanation.surface: A cook says a rice dish used to be good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' is not 'good' but a monetary penalty: in old Irish law an eric was the blood-money paid by a killer to the victim's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Under early Irish Brehon law, the compensation payment exacted for homicide was a historical penalty of this name.

indicators.note: the extremes of the word dirty are its first and last letters, so only those are taken

parts.note: unpleasant means nasty

explanation.surface: Someone describes a filthy, disagreeable home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is a royal or ruling family, as in the House of Windsor, not a building; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling family line such as the Tudors is called a house, and a succession of such rulers is the same thing.

parts.note: half of the word Friday, the day, is its first three letters FRI, also its standard abbreviation
a closing is an end
reduced means less, smaller in amount

explanation.surface: A shop with early closing on a half day has cut its hours and been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half day closing' suggests British early-closing day, when shops shut at lunchtime; here it splits into three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abandoned by everyone is left without companions or allies.

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny in British money
princely means royal, befitting a prince

explanation.surface: A stammered 'princely' sum minted at the Royal Mint.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'P-princely' separates P from 'princely'; 'mint' is the herb, not a place where coins are made.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic plant is a species of the herb genus Mentha, related to spearmint and peppermint.

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of clarinets being played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A deft musician with nimble fingers plays the clarinets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light-fingered' in the surface praises a woodwind player's touch, but it means given to stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-fingered person pilfers, and a thief is someone who commits larceny.

clue.text: Generator is put back by engineers

indicators.note: put back tells us the little word is is written in reverse order

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: Someone reports that engineers have pushed back a power generator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generator' suggests a machine, but here it is one who generates offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A male animal that fathers young, especially a stallion, is the one that begets or produces them.

parts.note: to sup is to drink, sip
porter is a dark, strong beer

explanation.surface: A football fan is able to drink strong beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan of a team or cause is a backer or follower of it.

clue.text: One raises the issue at meal-times

definitions.text: One raises the issue at meal-times

parts.words: One raises the issue at meal-times
parts.note: the issue is a child, offspring, lifted up to table height by a seat while the family eats

explanation.surface: Someone always brings up an awkward subject over dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raises the issue' sounds like broaching a topic; the issue is the baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall infant seat with a tray lifts a small child to the level of the table for eating.

clue.text: Unpleasant old woman, Georgia, retired with Henry

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A nasty old woman has retired to Georgia with a man named Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: A crone or witch-like ugly elderly female is called this.

definitions.note: beg is a verb while the answer is a noun, an appeal; the definition is loose

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words of the street name

explanation.surface: Someone goes begging in a suburban street.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to make an earnest appeal or entreaty to someone.

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
p, a penny, is a coin

explanation.surface: A copper coin is offered as a prize in a sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: Prizes such as the FA one are often silver goblets awarded to the winners.

clue.text: Stardust, for example, to glisten oddly

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters of to glisten arranged in a strange order

explanation.surface: Stardust is said to glitter strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stardust' is the Hoagy Carmichael standard, not cosmic dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is the name of a famous popular song, so it is an example of what a tune is called.

clue.text: Tamworth, for example, is affected by this news if ever bad

definitions.text: Tamworth, for example, is affected by this

indicators.note: bad news suggests the letters of news if ever are spoiled and jumbled

explanation.surface: A Staffordshire town hears the worst news ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a town in Staffordshire but also a British breed of pig, which is what is affected.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tamworth is a pig, and this is a contagious disease of pigs such as classical swine fever.

parts.note: a butter here is an animal that butts, and the gentler sex of that farm animal is the female

explanation.surface: A dairy asks which of its farm butters is softer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but something that butts with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the horned farm animal that butts is known by a name also used for a child's nurse.

clue.text: Four-letter word from Peg rising around ten to start with

indicators.note: around tells us the reversed name wraps round the next letter
in a down clue rising means the name is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret

indicators.note: to start with picks only the first letter of ten

explanation.surface: Peg gets up at ten to begin a word game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MARGARET into TERAGRAM, which goes 'around' T, the start of 'ten'.
explanation.definitionFit: From Greek tetra (four) and gramma (letter), it names a word of four letters, especially the Hebrew name of God.

clue.text: Chances of being divine in outsize jacket?

indicators.note: in tells us the divine is placed inside the outsize jacket

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine, a clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about the likelihood of looking godlike in a huge coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jacket' reinforces the containment: the clergyman is wrapped in OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting chances are expressed as a ratio, the probability of something happening.

clue.text: Soft brown coal left to burn

parts.note: to ignite is to set burning

explanation.surface: Brown coal is left in the grate to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the geological name for a low-grade, crumbly, brownish fuel between peat and true coal.

clue.text: Dealer who does not get the sack these days?

definitions.text: Dealer who does not get the sack these days?

parts.words: Dealer who does not get the sack these days?
parts.note: sack is an old name for a dry white wine such as sherry, which a wine merchant no longer stocks

explanation.surface: A trader is safe from being fired nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the sack' sounds like being dismissed, but sack is the old fortified wine Falstaff loved.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine merchant sells wine, and sack was a wine once sold widely.

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a figure is a form or shape

explanation.surface: An instruction to act in every role and for each figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on stage is to play a part before an audience.

definitions.meaning: jolly as an adverb means extremely, as in jolly good
a ... light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol, named after Edward ...

explanation.surface: A cheerful lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly means extremely in British speech, and a pyrotechnic signal flare is named after its American inventor.

clue.text: Openings for super rate of exchange

indicators.note: exchange suggests the letters of super rate swapping places

explanation.surface: A premium exchange rate creates opportunities for traders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate of exchange' reads as one financial phrase, but 'rate' is fodder and 'of exchange' the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Holes or gaps, such as the camera's adjustable lens hole, are openings.

clue.text: Treat from some of you, seemingly

indicators.note: some of tells us only a portion of the following words is taken, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A treat comes from some of your friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' picks letters running across 'you, seemingly'; the comma is ignored as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a tool or person in a certain way is to employ or handle them.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: gaga means foolish, senile, fatuous

explanation.surface: A nearly silly joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian's line or wisecrack is a quip.

clue.text: Devil with no tail in march?

indicators.note: with no tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a devil is a demon

explanation.surface: A tailless devil joins a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'march' is a protest march, not a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest procession is a demonstration, shortened to this.

definitions.meaning: a testimonial from a former employer
relation in the sense of bearing on something, as in 'with regard to'

explanation.surface: A family member writes a testimonial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' suggests a relative; it means connection or bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A testimonial supports a job applicant, and 'with respect to' something expresses connection to it.

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a game
in means at home

explanation.surface: A team collapses during a home game.
explanation.definitionFit: Collapse means downfall or destruction, as of a building.

explanation.surface: Horses and badgers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired old steeds have this name, and someone who persistently pesters someone does the same thing.

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: shouts means yells

explanation.surface: Builders shout to stop work on an extension.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US an ell is a wing at right angles to a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing built at right angles to the main house is named after the L shape it makes.

annotationWithheld.why: Balance of power established (4) as held: REST is 'balance', but no reading of 'of power established' gives REST or a second definition; likely an OCR or garbled clue

clue.text: Gambling system needs something to put on a horse

definitions.meaning: a betting strategy of doubling the stake after every loss

definitions.text: something to put on a horse
definitions.meaning: a strap of harness that stops a horse throwing its head up

explanation.surface: A betting plan requires a bet on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on a horse' sounds like placing a bet, but means fitting tack.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubling-up betting strategy shares its name with a harness strap running from noseband to girth.
